status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the full Geneva 1560 text at Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/exodus_2.json directly (all 40 chapters skimmed, key sections read in full: chs 1-11 birth/call/plagues, ch 15 Miriam's song, ch 17 Amalek battle, ch 18 Jethro's counsel, ch 24 elders on Sinai, chs 31/35-39 Bezaleel/Aholiab and the tabernacle craftsmen). Content is substantively IDENTICAL to the KJV account already indexed at Assets/Resources/Bible/CharacterIndex/Exodus.json — same events, same named figures, same order — differing only in archaic 1560 spelling/orthography (e.g. 'Iethro' for Jethro, 'Ioshua' for Joshua, 'Iaakob' for Jacob, 'Ebrewes' for Hebrews, 'moraine' for murrain). Per the task's own guidance, adapted the KJV's proven 10-tier structure rather than inventing a new one, but every verse reference and character detail below was re-verified against this translation's own text, not copied blind. Real spelling variants confirmed directly: Reuel/Iethro dual-naming (Exodus 2:18 vs 3:1, matching the KJV Reuel/Jethro flag), Miriam explicitly called 'the prophetesse' (15:20), the Amalek battle naming Ioshua/Aaron/Hur exactly as KJV does (17:9-13), Jethro's judicial-delegation counsel (18:13-27), Nadab/Abihu/Eleazar/Ithamar as Aaron's four sons via Elisheba daughter of Amminadab (6:23), and Bezaleel/Aholiab as the tabernacle's chief craftsmen (31:2-6, 35:30-35). NAMING-COLLISION FLAG (new observation, not present in the KJV draft's notes): the text names a second, distinct 'Hur' as Bezaleel's grandfather ('Bezaleel the sonne of Vri, the sonne of Hur of the tribe of Iudah' — 31:2, 35:30, 38:22) — the Geneva text itself never states this is the same Hur who held up Moses' hands with Aaron at Rephidim (17:10-12); a common Jewish tradition (sometimes tied to Miriam as his wife) asserts they're one man, but that identification is NOT made by the text itself, so this draft keeps them as two separate, unlinked entries rather than merging — same discipline as the Jethro/Bithiah precedent. Character ids suffixed _geneva throughout per the schema's translation-scoping instruction.

characters.name: Moses

verses.note: Born a Levite, hidden three months, set in an ark of reeds among the bulrushes, drawn out and named by Pharaoh's daughter ('because, said she, I drewe him out of the water')
The Angel of the Lord appears in the burning bush at Horeb; God reveals the name 'I Am That I Am'
Confronts Pharaoh with Aaron through the plagues (aged 80 at the confrontation, per 7:7)
Stretches out his hand and the Lord divides the Red Sea
His raised hands (steadied by Aaron and Hur) determine the outcome of the battle with Amalek
Receives the Ten Commandments
His face shines after speaking with God

funFacts: Nursed as an infant by his own mother Jochebed, hired by Pharaoh's daughter without her knowing the family relation (Exodus 2:7-9).

characters.name: Aaron

verses.note: Appointed as Moses' spokesman ('he shall be, euen he shall be as thy mouth')
Casts down his rod before Pharaoh; it becomes a serpent and devours the enchanters' rods
With Hur, holds up Moses' hands at the battle with Amalek
Consecrated as the first high priest
Fashions the golden calf under pressure from the people

funFacts: Three years older than Moses (Exodus 7:7); does the actual speaking to Pharaoh per the Lord's arrangement in 4:16.

characters.name: Zipporah

verses.note: Moses defends her and her sisters at the well in Midian and is given her in marriage by her father
Circumcises her son with a sharp knife at the inn, turning away the Lord's anger from Moses — 'Thou art indeede a bloody husband vnto me'
Jethro brings her and her sons to Moses in the wilderness after she had been sent away

funFacts: Not to be confused with Asenath, Joseph's Egyptian wife in Genesis 41:45 — two different women, a full book apart.

characters.name: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)

verses.note: 'There rose vp a newe King in Egypt, who knewe not Ioseph' — begins the oppression
Refuses Moses and Aaron's first request to let Israel go
Repeatedly hardens his heart through the plagues
Pursues Israel to the Red Sea; his army destroyed

funFacts: Never given a personal name in the text, same as the KJV account — a different, also-unnamed man from Joseph's Pharaoh in Genesis.

characters.name: Miriam

verses.note: Watches the ark in the reeds (unnamed as 'his sister' in this scene) and arranges for Jochebed to nurse Moses
Named directly and called 'the prophetesse, sister of Aaron' — leads the women with timbrels and dances after the Red Sea

funFacts: Explicitly titled 'the prophetesse' in Exodus 15:20 — one of the first women in scripture given that title outright.

characters.name: Joshua

verses.note: First appearance in scripture — Moses tells him to 'chuse vs out men, and go fight with Amalek' at Rephidim; wins while Moses' hands are held up
Called 'his minister' and goes up part of Mount Sinai with Moses
Does not depart out of the Tabernacle

funFacts: Rendered 'Ioshua' throughout this translation's spelling, the same figure as KJV's Joshua.

characters.name: Hur

verses.note: With Aaron, physically holds up Moses' hands on a stone seat through the whole battle with Amalek — 'so his hands were steady vntill the going downe of the sunne'
Left in charge of the people with Aaron while Moses is on Sinai

funFacts: Promoted to a full manager since the text makes his physical support the deciding factor in the battle's outcome, same reasoning as the KJV draft.

characters.name: Jethro

verses.note: Priest of Midian; gives Zipporah to Moses in marriage after Moses waters his flock
Brings Moses' wife and sons to him in the wilderness and offers sacrifice
Advises Moses to appoint rulers of thousands/hundreds/fifties/tens to share the burden of judging

funFacts: Also called Reuel earlier in the same book (Exodus 2:18) — flagged rather than silently merged, same as the KJV entry: most likely one man known by two names/titles.

characters.name: Bezaleel

verses.note: 'Filled...with the spirit of God, in wisdome, and in vnderstanding, and in knowledge, and in all workmanship' — the tabernacle's chief craftsman
Named again as construction begins, paired with Aholiab
Builds the Ark, the altar, and the tabernacle's furnishings

funFacts: Called 'the sonne of Vri, the sonne of Hur of the tribe of Iudah' (31:2) — a naming-collision flag, NOT merged here with the Hur of Exodus 17, since the text never states they are the same man (see the book-level notes).

characters.name: Aholiab

verses.note: Given by name alongside Bezaleel to help build the tabernacle
Named 'sonne of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, a cunning workeman and an embroiderer and a worker of needle work'

funFacts: Of the tribe of Dan — paired with Bezaleel (tribe of Judah) across the one shared project.

verses.note: 'Amram tooke Iochebed his fathers sister to his wife...bare him Aaron and Moses' — of the tribe of Levi
Hides Moses three months, then is hired (unnamed in the scene) to nurse her own son for Pharaoh's daughter
Named directly as Amram's wife, 'his fathers sister'
Named — 'I haue bene a stranger in a strange lande'
Named among Moses' sons brought by Jethro; his name recalls 'the God of my father...deliuered me from the sword of Pharaoh'
Goes up part of Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Abihu, and seventy elders
Named among those consecrated as priests with Aaron
Goes up part of Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and seventy elders
Named among those consecrated as priests with Aaron
One of two named Hebrew midwives who defy Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys; 'God therefore prospered the midwiues'
The second of the two named Hebrew midwives who defy Pharaoh
Unnamed as 'the enchaunters'/'the sorcerers' — replicate some of Moses and Aaron's signs, then fail
New Testament cross-reference explicitly names Jannes and Jambres as the ones who withstood Moses
Unnamed as 'the enchaunters'/'the sorcerers'
New Testament cross-reference names Jannes and Jambres directly
Named as Aaron's wife, 'sister of Nahashon'

characters.name: Eleazar

verses.note: Named among Aaron's four sons
Takes a wife of the daughters of Putiel, who bears him Phinehas

funFacts: Not yet prominent in Exodus itself — becomes far more significant after Nadab and Abihu die in Leviticus.

verses.note: Named among Aaron's four sons

characters.name: Phinehas (Eleazar's son)

verses.note: Born to Eleazar; the text notes 'these are the principall fathers of the Leuites throughout their families'

funFacts: Named only here in Exodus as a genealogical entry — his own major role (the zealous act at Baal-peor) comes later, in Numbers.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

jethroOtherDaughters.note: 'The Priest of Midian had seue daughters' — only Zipporah is named; the other six are not.

pharaohsDaughter.note: Never named in this translation, same as KJV. Not asserted to be 'Bithiah' (1 Chronicles 4:18) — that identification is a later tradition, not something this text states.
